Draw locations from location surfaces

Source: R/sample_locations.R
sample_locations.Rd

Draws cells from location surfaces in proportion to their probability, with replacement, for analyses that take points rather than surfaces, such as habitat selection.

Usage

sample_locations(surface, n, seed = NULL)

Arguments

surface

A location surface from location_surface().

n

Number of draws per animal and bin.

seed

An integer seed for the draws, or NULL to use the current random number stream. The caller's stream is restored afterwards when a seed is given.

Value

A data frame with one row per draw: animal_id, bin_start (the bin the draw came from), draw, cell, x and y (the cell centre in the grid's coordinates, NA when the surface holds no grid). Attributes: "estimand" and "epsg", the grid's EPSG code.

Details

Draws are with replacement, so a cell is drawn as often as its probability says; a draw without replacement would push draws out of the most probable cells once those were taken. Each draw is the centre of its cell. Only the kept cells of a surface can be drawn (see location_surface()); their probabilities are rescaled to sum to one. n cells are drawn for each animal and bin, so the draws describe the animal's location in its detected bins only.

See also

location_surface(), credible_region()

Examples

tif <- system.file("extdata", "stoney_depth.tif", package = "detfield")
grid <- terra::rast(tif)
# Beyond 2 km the Stoney curve is below 0.001 at every receiver; leaving
# those pairs out keeps the example quick.
dist <- water_distances(grid, stoney_track$receivers,
                        max_distance = 2000)
model <- de_logistic(d50 = c(250, 750), d05 = c(500, 1500), depth = c(1, 35))
field <- de_field(dist, de_model(model, sigma = list(station_hour = 0)))
#> 194 of 7,669 receiver-cell pairs with p >= 0.05 have land on the
#>   straight line between them; with blocked = 0 the curve is read on
#>   them as if the line were clear. See `blocked` in ?de_model.
counts <- bin_detections(stoney_track$detections, stoney_track$receivers,
                         stoney_track$tags)
surface <- location_surface(counts, field)
head(sample_locations(surface, n = 100, seed = 1))
#>   animal_id           bin_start draw cell      x       y
#> 1 stoney-01 2024-06-01 04:00:00    1 2502 735254 4940491
#> 2 stoney-01 2024-06-01 04:00:00    2 2503 735354 4940491
#> 3 stoney-01 2024-06-01 04:00:00    3 2670 735254 4940391
#> 4 stoney-01 2024-06-01 04:00:00    4 2837 735154 4940291
#> 5 stoney-01 2024-06-01 04:00:00    5 2335 735354 4940591
#> 6 stoney-01 2024-06-01 04:00:00    6 2837 735154 4940291
